item.title: Exploiting React Native Apps: A Hands-On Walkthrough with DVRN
item.description:
This is Part 2 of a two-part series on testing React Native applications. Part 1 covered identifying an RN app, detecting its architecture and JS engine, and reading its bundle. This part puts all of that to use against DVRN, a deliberately vulnerable RN app I built specifically for this series, walking through five real vulnerabilities end to end.

Introducing DVRN

DVRN (Damn Vulnerable React Native) is a deliberately vulnerable React Native app I built to have a real, hands-on target for the techniques covered in Part 1, rather than talking about them in the abstract.

item.title: Understanding React Native Apps: A Pentester's Field Guide
item.description:
This is Part 1 of a two-part series on testing React Native applications. This part covers what you need to know before you start testing- identifying an RN app, understanding how it’s actually built, and setting up the right recon workflow. Part 2 walks through exploiting five real vulnerabilities using DVRN, a deliberately vulnerable RN app I built specifically for this series.

What is React Native, and why should a pentester care

React Native lets you write mobile apps in JavaScript, using React, and ship them as genuinely native Android and iOS apps. That last part matters more than it sounds. Instead of compiling your code into a web browser wrapper like traditional hybrid apps, it communicates directly with the host platform - your <View> and <Text> components become real android.widget.* views on Android, not HTML rendered inside a WebView. The JS layer decides what to show and how to respond to events; the actual rendering is native.

item.title: Chaining Deep Link Injection with SQLi to Leak Sensitive Data from an iOS App
item.description:
This is my writeup for the Flipcoin Wallet iOS challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - a two-part challenge involving deep link abuse and SQL injection that chains together really nicely.

Understanding the Challenge

The app is a crypto banking app with Flipcoin as its currency. Features:

  • Receive coins via QR code
  • Send coins to other accounts
  • Transaction history
  • Crypto news tab

The challenge description mentions SQLi and deeplink exploitation. The goal is to extract recovery keys of other users.

item.title: Defeating Multi-Layer Anti-Reversing Protections on iOS with Static Analysis and Frida
item.description:
This is my writeup for the Captain NoHook iOS challenge by Mobile Hacking Labs - combining multiple runtime checks, a non-exported debugger trap, and a hidden flag buried in memory.

Overview

A classic mobile RASP / anti-reversing puzzle. Goal: bypass the app’s reverse-engineering/compliance checks and find the hidden flag in memory.

Combined static analysis (radare2 / nm) with dynamic instrumentation (Frida) and Objection for memory inspection.

1. Static Discovery with r2 / nm

Loaded the app binary into r2 and searched for symbols/functions containing the term compliant. That quickly pointed at the high-level check deciding whether the device is “noncompliant”.
